title: The Day the Moon Swapped the Salt
skyStory: A sly waning crescent, barely a quarter lit, is lounging in Aquarius with a whoopee cushion and absolutely no remorse. Aquarius invented the clever prank and has been waiting all year for permission. Saturn has hidden the remote. Mars has taped a googly eye to the kettle. The moon swears it was not involved, which is exactly what a prankster says.

reading: Somebody will try to fool you before 10:40 am, and you will see it coming from a kilometre away. Here is the twist: fall for it anyway, loudly, with a gasp worthy of the stage. The [[Six of Pentacles]] says receiving a prank gracefully counts as receiving.

The Fire Tiger is built for pouncing, so plan one gentle prank of your own and keep it kind. Think a sticky note on a stapler that reads I have feelings too, or a rubber duck where the mouse should be. Nothing that costs anyone a minute of real work. The universe grades pranks on joy per second, and Life Path 3 is famous for its timing.
joel.mission: Turn one ordinary object on a shared desk upside down and wait to see who notices first, then confess with a bow.
joel.omen: A clock that is exactly one hour wrong. It means the day is playing along with you, so lean into the bit.

reading: Nobody fools a Wood Rat. You will spot three pranks in progress before lunch, including one aimed at someone else, and you will say nothing. Silence is the most powerful seat in the theatre.

Around 2:30 pm you get to decide whether to warn the target or let the joke land. Let it land, then be the first to laugh, which turns a prank into a party. Later, tell the story of it with your hands, adding one small detail that did not happen. The Life Path 11 in you knows a tale grows best with a little fertiliser, and today is the one day it is allowed.
nancy.mission: Tell someone a completely true fact so outlandish they assume it is an April Fools joke, and refuse to back down.
nancy.omen: A lone sock on the floor where no sock should be. Someone is pranking you, and they are bad at it.

together.text: Each send the other a fake fortune today, written like an official cosmic memo, with a stamp drawn in pen. The best line wins bragging rights until May. The moon will be reading over both shoulders, and it has notes on your comedic timing.

title: The Great Puddle Census
skyStory: The crescent has shrunk to a fifth of itself and is still in Aquarius, sorting the clouds into committees. April in Atlantic Canada has delivered its finest product: puddles, in quantity. The moon has volunteered to count them. Saturn says this is not a real job. The moon has already reached four hundred and twelve and refuses to stop.

reading: Mud season has arrived at the cabin, and the boots by the door look like they lost a wrestling match. That is fine. Mud is just earth that is excited about spring, and you know a thing or two about being excited about everything at once.

The [[Knight of Wands]] asks you to aim your fire at a single task today, ideally one that has been sitting in a drawer since February. Open the drawer. Look it in the eye. Finish one honest piece of it before 3 pm and leave the rest folded for tomorrow. When someone asks how your day went, give them a one-word answer and watch them try to decode it.
joel.mission: Step in exactly one puddle on purpose today, with full commitment, like a kid who has never heard of socks.
joel.omen: A worm crossing a sidewalk. It means slow progress still counts, so keep inching toward the thing.

reading: The shore smells like thaw today, salt and wet stone and something green getting ideas. Stand still for a moment and let it register. A Capricorn knows that seasons turn whether or not anyone signs the paperwork.

Someone near you will be stuck on a problem around mid-afternoon, and you will see the answer the way a Wood Rat sees a crumb under the couch. Do not hand it over. Ask them one perfect question instead and watch their face light up as they find it themselves. Leveling people up is your favourite sport, and today you score from the sidelines.
nancy.mission: Find the biggest puddle on your route and give it a dignified name, then use that name in conversation later.
nancy.omen: A crow riding a swaying power line like it is nothing. Balance is easier than it looks, so stop overthinking the next step.

together.text: Send each other a photo of the muddiest thing you see today, no caption. Score it out of ten for drama. Saturn will claim to be above this contest but secretly keeps the spreadsheet, and the moon has bet on Nancy.

title: The Fog Machine Is On Again
skyStory: Down to a slim twelve percent, the crescent has slipped into Pisces, the dreamy fish sign, and immediately switched on the fog machine. The whole coast looks like a stage before the band comes out. Pisces loves a mood. Saturn wants to know who approved the budget for atmosphere. Nobody did. The fog is freelance.

reading: Visibility is low and that is a gift. When you cannot see the whole road, you are only allowed to think about the next ten metres, and the next ten metres are very manageable.

Around 11:15 am an idea will arrive half-formed, like a shape in the fog. Write it down without finishing it. Pisces says unfinished ideas are allowed to stay soft for a while. Later today someone offers to help with a chore you were going to do alone. The [[Six of Pentacles]] is wearing a raincoat and nodding at you. Say yes and let the cabin smoke curl up into the grey.
joel.mission: Draw a tiny tiger in the fog on a window or mirror and leave it there for someone to find.
joel.omen: A foghorn or any low sound that repeats. It means steady signals beat loud ones, so keep showing up.

reading: The fog has rolled right up to the edge of the woods, and the shore feels like a secret only you know about. You do your best thinking when the world gets quiet like this.

The [[Six of Swords]] drifts by in the mist today, a small boat with a lantern on the bow. You do not need to see the far shore to keep rowing. You only need the lantern. Pick one small thing you have been carrying and set it down on the dock this afternoon. It will still be there tomorrow if you want it, but you probably will not.
nancy.mission: Stand somewhere foggy for one full minute and invent the plot of a mystery novel set exactly there.
nancy.omen: A light on in a window you usually see dark. It means someone is awake to your idea, so share it.

together.text: Each write three words describing the fog where you are and swap them at dusk. If any word matches, the fog has been gossiping between your two coasts. If none match, write three more. The fish of Pisces is holding the lantern and enjoying this immensely.

title: The Matching Sand Shovels Incident
skyStory: A thread of a crescent, only six percent awake, floats in Pisces like a fish fin glimpsed under dark water. Pisces deals in echoes and doubles, and tonight it is feeling generous. Two things that should not match will match. Saturn is checking its notes twice. Mars is pretending not to have arranged anything. The fin flicks once.

reading: Today the universe runs a copy machine. Something you say before noon will be repeated, word for word, by a total stranger before supper. You will want to scream. Don't even scream. Just write it down with the time.

The Tiger usually pounces first and asks questions later, but the echo wants you still. When the repeat happens, take it as a nudge that the idea you have been circling is worth one real step this week. Not ten steps. One. Life Path 3 loves an audience, and today the cosmos is the audience, quietly repeating your lines back to you so you hear how good they sound.
joel.mission: Pick an unusual word at breakfast, something like marmalade or lighthouse, and count how many times it shows up today.
joel.omen: Two pigeons on a ledge turning their heads in perfect unison. You are in sync with something bigger, so trust today's hunch.

reading: You will find a child's plastic sand shovel poking out of a melting snowbank this morning, the kind of spring relic winter gives back. Remember its colour. By 4 pm you will see its exact twin somewhere else entirely.

This is the kind of thing only a Wood Rat notices, and that is the point. Your eye for the tiny detail is the whole trick of Life Path 11. When the second shovel appears, tell someone the story with both hands, and watch them not believe you. Then text Joel the colour. He will reply with something that matches, and you will both say the same three letters at once.
nancy.mission: Photograph any lost toy you spot today, a shovel, a ball, a tiny truck, and give it a hopeful name, like it is waiting for a reunion.
nancy.omen: A song playing in two different places within an hour. It means the echo has found you too.

together.text: DES day, officially. Each of you guess one random object the other will see today: a blue bucket, a cat in a window, a kite stuck in a tree. Swap guesses at noon, report back at dark. If either guess lands, ΔΕΣ is written in the sky.

title: The Blank Page Has Opinions
skyStory: New moon in Pisces, two percent lit, which is to say the sky has turned its face to the wall to think. A new moon is a blank notebook, and Pisces has bought the fancy kind with the ribbon bookmark. Saturn wants a table of contents before anyone writes a word. The moon says hush and uncaps a pen.

reading: New moons are for intentions, and you have about forty. The trick tonight is to write only one on paper and let the other thirty-nine stay in your head where they can keep each other company.

Make it something small enough to finish by the next new moon. Not a kingdom, a doorway. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] wants a slow plan, the kind with steady hooves. Around 7 pm, with the cabin quiet and the chimney ticking, read your one line out loud to the empty room. Rooms remember things. Then put the paper somewhere you will stumble upon it in three weeks.
joel.mission: Write one intention on a scrap of paper and hide it inside a book you will reread this year.
joel.omen: A blank wall that catches a slice of evening light. It means there is space for the new thing, so start it.

reading: The tide goes way out on a new moon, further than usual, showing rocks and shells nobody has seen all winter. Your mind does the same tonight. Old ideas you forgot about are suddenly visible again.

Pick one up and turn it over. Is it a shell worth keeping or just a pretty stone? You will know within ten seconds; you always do. [[The Sun]] card is not in the sky tonight, but it sits reversed in your spread for a reason. Joy does not need earning. Let yourself be pleased with an idea simply because it is yours, and set the ruby beside it like a guard.
nancy.mission: Light one candle tonight and write a single word on a sticky note beside it. Keep the note for a month.
nancy.omen: A shell, button or bead in an unexpected spot. It means a forgotten plan is ready to come back.

together.text: Trade intentions tonight, one line each, no explanations allowed. Then each guard the other's intention like a dragon guards gold: ask about it once a week until the next new moon. Saturn will act as notary. Saturn loves a notary job.

title: The Ram Kicks Open the Door
skyStory: The moon is completely dark, zero percent, and it has just walked into Aries, Joel's own sign, without knocking. Aries is a ram, and rams do not knock. Mars, who runs Aries, has rolled out a red carpet made of construction paper. Saturn watches from across the street, sipping something warm, saying nothing, quietly impressed.

reading: The new moon is visiting your sign, which in Fire Tiger terms means the house has been tidied, the lights are low, and the cosmos is waiting to see what you will do first. Pressure? No. Invitation.

You will feel the pull to start three projects by lunch. Start one and give it a ridiculous name, the more dramatic the better, like Operation Thunder Shelf. The [[Knight of Wands]] loves a code name. By 5 pm, do one physical thing for it: buy nothing, but move something, sketch something, or clear one surface. Rams are built for the first push, and you were born on the first day of spring.
joel.mission: Give today's main task a heroic code name and use it in at least two sentences out loud.
joel.omen: A door propped open with something odd, like a shoe or a brick. It means the way is clear, so walk through.

reading: With the moon in Aries, Joel's energy is spilling over the edges of the map, and some of it will land in your lap around 1 pm as a message with too many exclamation marks. Enjoy it.

You are the mountain, and mountains are good at weather. Let his spark bounce off you and send back one calm sentence that makes the plan twice as good. The Wood Rat in you will see the tiny flaw nobody else noticed, the missing screw in the bookshelf. Mention it kindly. Then switch on your own small fire: one task you have been patient about for too long. Today it gets your full attention.
nancy.mission: Reply to the most enthusiastic message you get today with an equally enthusiastic one, matching exclamation mark for exclamation mark.
nancy.omen: A red ribbon or red string caught on something. It means the Aries moon is tugging your sleeve, so say yes once.

together.text: Joel's sign is hosting the moon, so Joel picks a tiny challenge and Nancy has to accept it before supper. Something like naming five birds or writing a four-line poem about a spoon. Tomorrow Nancy picks the counter-challenge. Mars is refereeing and is very biased.

title: The Day of the Borrowed Courage
skyStory: One percent of a moon, a hair of silver, still lounging in Aries like a houseguest who found the good blanket. The ram is restless. It wants to charge something, anything. Mars suggests the laundry pile. Saturn suggests patience. The moon splits the difference and charges the laundry pile very patiently.

reading: Yesterday you lit the fuse. Today is about tending the flame instead of throwing more logs on it. Check on Operation Whatever-You-Named-It and add one tidy piece, not a whole new wing.

A neighbour, coworker or stranger in a rain jacket will compliment something you made around 12:20 pm. Your reflex is to say oh, it was nothing. The [[Six of Pentacles]] has posted a sign on the cabin door: no deflecting. Say thank you and let it sit there like a warm mug. Then go outside, find the first crocus poking up, and tell it that it is doing great too.
joel.mission: Accept three compliments today with a plain thank you, no jokes, no explanations, no returns.
joel.omen: The first crocus you see this year. It means effort has broken through the frost, so celebrate something.

reading: The Aries moon lends you a pocketful of Joel's nerve today. Borrow it. You have been sitting on a question, a request, a small ask, and the ram says go.

Ask it before 2 pm, plainly, without a wind-up paragraph. Saturn, your ruler, has agreed to step out for coffee and let Mars drive for one afternoon. The [[Strength]] card hums in the background, lion and gentle hand. You do not have to roar. A Capricorn with a clear ask is already a little terrifying, in the best way. Afterwards, walk to the edge of the water and breathe.
nancy.mission: Make one small request you have been putting off, in a single sentence, before 2 pm.
nancy.omen: A dog pulling hard on its leash toward something. It means go after what you want today.

together.text: Nancy's counter-challenge day. She picks something Joel must do before bedtime, and it must involve receiving help, a favour or a gift of time. Joel is not allowed to repay it this week. Mars is grumbling. Saturn is delighted. The moon is taking notes.

title: The Bull Wants a Nap
skyStory: Three percent of a moon has drifted from Aries into Taurus, and the energy changes from a sprint to a sofa. Taurus is the bull who would rather smell the flowers than charge the cape. The moon has kicked off its boots, propped up its feet, and requested a blanket. Mars is pacing. Saturn approves wholeheartedly.

reading: After two days of charging around, the cosmos is ordering you to sit on the porch of the cabin and do nothing for at least fifteen minutes. This is not a suggestion; it is a summons.

You will feel guilty around minute four. Ignore it. The [[Four of Swords]] is lying on a stone bench nearby with its hands folded, looking extremely relaxed. Rest is how embers get hot enough to last. While you sit, notice one sound you have never paid attention to, maybe a dripping eave or the creak of a branch. That sound is the theme song for the rest of your week.
joel.mission: Sit outside or by an open window for fifteen minutes with nothing in your hands, and count three birds.
joel.omen: A cat stretched in a sunbeam. It means rest is productive today, so take the hint seriously.

reading: Taurus is an earth sign, like you, and the moon has come to your neighbourhood for a slow visit. Take your time with everything today. Walk at a third of your usual speed for one block and watch the world catch up.

Around 3:45 pm, something small and beautiful will happen near you: a ribbon of light on a wall, a child laughing at a squirrel, steam curling from a mug. The Wood Rat sees it, of course. Tell one person about it with your full storytelling hands, turning a three-second moment into a two-minute saga. They will thank you later for slowing them down too.
nancy.mission: Describe one tiny beautiful thing you saw today to someone, using at least three hand gestures.
nancy.omen: Steam rising from somewhere unexpected. It means something warm is brewing for you, so be patient.

together.text: No challenges today. Instead, each send a photo of the coziest corner you can find, with a single word describing how it feels. The bull will judge the coziest. The bull always picks the one with a blanket in it.

title: The Snowbank Gives Back
skyStory: The young moon is waxing, eight percent lit, still grazing in Taurus with a mouthful of clover. As the light grows, the last snowbanks shrink and start returning lost items to their owners: a glove, a toy shovel, one extremely confused tennis ball. Taurus files the items carefully. Saturn has opened a lost and found desk.

reading: Something you lost or forgot about this winter will turn up today. Maybe a tool, maybe an idea, maybe a promise you made to yourself in January when everything was dark.

When it appears, do not just pocket it. Ask why it came back now. The Fire Tiger hunts best when it pauses to sniff the wind first. The [[Ace of Wands]] is sprouting a leaf somewhere near you, meaning an old spark is ready to grow again. Spend ten minutes on whatever returned before 6 pm. Then put it somewhere it will not get buried next winter.
joel.mission: Clear out one coat pocket you have not checked since winter and read whatever you find like a message.
joel.omen: Something bright revealed in a melting snowbank. It means an old idea is ready, so pick it up.

reading: The ice at the edge of the shore is breaking up into floating plates, clinking like dishes after a dinner party. That sound is the year changing its mind about winter.

You will be asked for advice twice today, once by someone close and once by someone you barely know. Give the stranger the longer answer. Life Path 11 is wired for these little crossings. The [[Six of Swords]] is on its way through the loose ice, and you are standing at the oar with a quiet grin. Whatever you have been carrying since February, notice how much lighter it already is.
nancy.mission: Leave a kind anonymous note somewhere public today, under a mug or on a bulletin board.
nancy.omen: Ice cracking or dripping loudly. It means a stuck situation is loosening, so give it one more nudge.

together.text: Each name one thing that came back to you this spring: a habit, a hobby, a laugh. Swap them by text with a single emoji-free sentence. The snowbank is giving things back, and so are you two. Saturn has stamped both items as returned.

title: The Twins Start a Group Chat
skyStory: Sixteen percent lit and climbing, the moon has bounded into Gemini, the twins, the sign that talks with both hands and texts with both thumbs. The sky is suddenly very chatty. Gemini has started a group chat with every star and named it Spring Plans. Saturn has muted it. Mars replied with forty-two messages in a row.

reading: Words are your instrument, Life Path 3, and Gemini just tuned every string. Messages flow easily today, maybe too easily. Before sending anything over four paragraphs, read it once out loud to the cabin walls.

Around 1:30 pm a conversation will veer off into a delightful tangent, something about birds or old cartoons or why spoons exist. Follow it for five minutes. The best ideas this week live in that tangent. The [[Page of Swords]] is lurking nearby with a notebook, writing down every clever thing you say. Ask it for a copy later.
joel.mission: Start a conversation with a question you have never asked anyone before, and listen to the whole answer.
joel.omen: Two birds chattering on a wire. It means a conversation today matters more than it seems, so pay attention.

reading: Your hands are going to be busy today. Gemini loves a storyteller, and you are about to be cast as the lead in at least three conversations before dinner.

One of them will be with someone who needs a push to level up. Do your thing: one well-aimed question, one story about a time you got unstuck, and a wink. The Wood Rat clocks the exact moment their eyes light up. Later, around 8 pm, write down the best sentence you said all day. Gemini insists it was very good, and Gemini is rarely wrong about sentences.
nancy.mission: Teach someone one small trick or shortcut you know, even if it seems too obvious to share.
nancy.omen: A notebook or scrap of paper left behind on a table. It means your words are needed, so write something.

together.text: Text each other only in questions for one full hour this evening. No statements allowed. The first one to accidentally say something that is not a question owes the other a ridiculous nickname for the weekend. Gemini is moderating and has already taken sides.

title: The Sunday of Two Opinions
skyStory: A quarter-lit crescent lingers in Gemini, and the twins cannot agree on anything. One twin wants a long walk. The other wants a long nap. They have been arguing since dawn and have both somehow won. Mars wants to settle it with a race. Saturn has quietly booked both activities in a sensible order.

reading: Two versions of your Sunday are competing for the throne: the one where you build something and the one where you lie on the floor listening to rain. Gemini says you can have both, as long as you pick the order on purpose.

Build first, before noon, with the [[Knight of Wands]] holding a single torch, not a bonfire. One shelf, one page, one fixed hinge. After lunch the Tiger is officially off duty. Lie down, stretch out, and let the afternoon pour over you like warm syrup. If guilt arrives, tell it you are following cosmic orders and it can file a complaint with the twins.
joel.mission: Write two to-do lists, one serious and one absurd, and complete one item from each before dark.
joel.omen: A fork in a path or a road with two signs. It means both choices are good today, so stop agonising.

reading: Two people will ask for your opinion on the same small thing today, and they want opposite answers. The Wood Rat smells the setup a mile off.

Here is the trick: give them both the same honest answer and let them sort it out. Patience is your quiet superpower, and today it has a mischievous streak. Later, around 4 pm, treat yourself to an hour with a story, read or told or overheard. Life Path 11 recharges through other people's tales. If the [[Two of Cups]] floats into your thoughts, call someone you have not talked to since winter.
nancy.mission: Ask two different people the same odd question, like what colour Tuesday is, and compare their answers.
nancy.omen: A pair of matching birds. It means a decision you feel split on is simpler than it looks.

together.text: Agree on one tiny thing to do at the same time this evening, wherever you are: step outside at 8:08 pm and look at the crescent for one minute. Gemini, the sign of pairs, will count it as a visit. Saturn will count it as a scheduled meeting.

title: The Soup Moon Rises
skyStory: The moon reaches first quarter, a neat half-lemon at thirty-five percent, and settles into Cancer, the crab who carries home on its back. Cancer wants everyone fed, warm, and accounted for. It has knitted a scarf for Mars. Mars is wearing it ironically. Saturn has been handed a ladle and is weirdly good at it.

reading: First quarter moons are decision points, and Cancer makes the decision about home. Today your best work happens at the cabin table, not out in the world.

Make the place nicer by one degree. Hang the picture that has leaned against the wall since autumn. Move the chair closer to the window. Light a candle at 6 pm even though it is still bright out. The [[Ten of Cups]] is drawing a rainbow over your roof, and it is a little crooked, like a kid made it. Fine. Crooked rainbows still count.
joel.mission: Fix, hang or move one thing at home that has bugged you since autumn, and admire it twice.
joel.omen: Smoke from a chimney drifting straight up. It means home is in balance, so stay in tonight.

reading: Cancer and Capricorn sit across from each other on the zodiac wheel, so tonight's moon is looking straight at you across the table. It wants to know: who looks after the one who looks after everyone?

The answer today is you. Make your own favourite warm thing, a drink, a blanket nest, a playlist of songs from the shore, and enjoy it without multitasking. When someone asks for help after 7 pm, say tomorrow, kindly. [[The Empress]] card is not in your spread, but she is here anyway, insisting you put your feet up. Mountains need rest days too.
nancy.mission: Spend twenty minutes doing something only for yourself, then tell no one about it. Keep it a secret treasure.
nancy.omen: A hermit crab or snail shell on a path or windowsill. It means your shell is allowed to be cozy today.

together.text: Describe your home to each other using only three smells. No pictures, no extra details. Then guess one thing in the other's kitchen right now. The crab moon is holding a wooden spoon and will judge accuracy with great tenderness.

title: The Identical Sandwich Prophecy
skyStory: Nearly half the moon is glowing now, forty-six percent, still curled up in Cancer like a crab in a teacup. Cancer has psychic tendencies and tonight it is showing off. It has arranged for something identical to happen in two kitchens a long way apart. Saturn calls it statistical noise. Mars calls it a sign. The crab simply clicks its claws.

reading: At lunchtime you will make or order something and think, huh, that is not what I usually pick. Take a photo of it. You will need evidence later.

By evening, Nancy will report having eaten exactly the same thing, on the same kind of plate, at roughly the same minute. Don't even scream. The Tiger and the Rat are running on the same clock today. Use it: anything you start this afternoon, mention it to her, because she is probably thinking about the same problem from the other side. [[The Lovers]] card here is about alignment, two minds choosing the same path.
joel.mission: Choose the third option on any menu or shelf today, no matter what it is, and take a picture.
joel.omen: The same number on two receipts or tickets. It means your timing is uncanny, so act on today's hunch.

reading: Something at lunch will make you laugh before you even taste it, maybe the shape of it or the way it sits on the plate. Photograph it from directly above, like a detective at a scene.

By 8 pm, Joel's photo will arrive and it will be the same lunch. Same angle. Possibly the same napkin. The Wood Rat sees patterns before anyone, and you will spot the match before he even types a word. Say it with your hands, even over text: ΔΕΣ. Then tell the story to one other person tomorrow. They will not believe you, and that is part of the fun.
nancy.mission: Photograph your lunch from directly above and send it to Joel before he sends his.
nancy.omen: Two people wearing identical jackets. It means the universe is copying and pasting today, so expect more.

together.text: DES day. Compare lunch photos at 8 pm sharp and score the match out of ten. A perfect ten means you both win a free cosmic upgrade, redeemable whenever. The crab moon is officiating, and it insists the napkins count.

title: The Lion Takes the Stage
skyStory: The moon has swollen past half, fifty-eight percent, and strutted into Leo, the lion, who has just discovered there is a spotlight and it is pointed at Leo. The moon is wearing a tiny gold cape. Mars is applauding from the front row. Saturn is in the back, arms crossed, but tapping one foot.

reading: Fire moon, fire sign, Fire Tiger. Today the stage is yours. When you speak in a meeting, a call, or at the counter of a busy shop, people will lean in. Life Path 3 was made for this.

Use it to lift someone else. Around 11 am, give public credit to a person who did quiet work nobody noticed. Name the specific thing. Watch them glow. [[The Sun]] card in your spread is reversed because you keep earning joy instead of allowing it, so here is your loophole: joy you give away bounces back with interest. Let it hit you. Do not duck.
joel.mission: Praise one person by name in front of others for something specific they did this month.
joel.omen: A cat sitting in a window like it owns the street. It means confidence is in the air, so speak up.

reading: The lion moon wants you to tell a story today, a real performance with pauses and hand flourishes. You know the one, the story that always gets a laugh. Tell it to someone new.

As the punchline lands, notice how they lean back, because that is the effect you have on rooms. Capricorns do not always want the spotlight, but Leo is lending you its cape for an afternoon, and it looks great on you. If the [[Queen of Wands]] appears in a daydream, take note: she has a cat at her feet and a sunflower in hand, and she looks a lot like you.
nancy.mission: Tell your best story to someone who has never heard it, and make it at least ten percent more dramatic.
nancy.omen: A sunflower, a gold ribbon, or anything bright yellow in a window. It means the stage is yours today.

together.text: Each record a ten-second voice message introducing the other as if they are walking onstage at a sold-out show. Big announcer voice. Include one made-up award they have won. The lion moon will be playing it on repeat.

title: The Day of the Backwards Hat
skyStory: At sixty-nine percent and swelling, the moon is still in Leo and has decided to wear its crown backwards, just to see who notices. Leo loves an entrance and a bit of swagger. The peepers have started singing in the marshes, and the lion assumes they are singing about it. Saturn does not have the heart to correct it.

reading: Yesterday you were on stage. Today the lion moon wants you backstage, checking the ropes. It is less glamorous, but the show depends on it.

Check one boring system you rely on: the batteries in the smoke detector, the stack of half-read mail, the drawer with forty mystery keys. Fix one. The [[Eight of Pentacles]] is sitting at a workbench nearby, sanding something patiently, humming along to the peepers. Craft is a kind of love. When you are done, walk outside after dark and listen. The marsh choir is louder than it was last week.
joel.mission: Sort one drawer of mystery objects at home and throw away exactly three things nobody will miss.
joel.omen: The peepers singing for the first time where you live. It means spring has officially signed in.

reading: You will see someone wearing something backwards or inside out today, and you will be the only one who notices. Do you tell them? The Wood Rat says yes, gently, with a wink.

That small kindness sets the tone for the whole day. Around 2 pm, you will have a chance to save someone from a tiny embarrassment, a typo, a loose tag, a forgotten coffee on a roof. Swoop in. The Leo moon makes you fearless today, but with a Capricorn's precision. You do not need applause. You will get a grateful look, and that is better.
nancy.mission: Gently tell one person about a tag sticking out, a typo, or a mug left behind, with a smile.
nancy.omen: A hat or cap left on a bench. It means someone needs your sharp eyes today, so look around.

together.text: Wear one item backwards or on the wrong side today, a hat, a sock, a bracelet, and see who notices first. Report at bedtime. If nobody does, the lion moon is personally offended and will be louder tomorrow.

title: The Clipboard Moon
skyStory: The moon has grown gibbous, seventy-nine percent and round-shouldered, and stepped into Virgo, the sign of tidy margins and alphabetised spices. It has arrived with a clipboard. Every star is being inspected. Leo has been asked to remove the cape. Mars is sulking. Saturn has never been happier and is helping with the checkboxes.

reading: Virgo is not your natural habitat, Fire Tiger, but it has something to teach you today: finishing. Pick one task that is ninety percent done and drag it across the line before 4 pm.

It will feel slow and fiddly. The last ten percent always does. That is where the [[Knight of Pentacles]] lives, plodding along on a horse who refuses to gallop. The horse is right. When the thing is truly done, celebrate with something ridiculous: a victory lap around the cabin, a cheer to the trees. Virgo will pretend not to be amused but is secretly writing gold star on its clipboard.
joel.mission: Finish one task that is ninety percent done, then do a short victory lap around your home.
joel.omen: A perfectly straight row of something, cans, birds, fence posts. It means order helps you today, so tidy up.

reading: Virgo is an earth sign, your kin. You and the moon will understand each other perfectly today, two practical minds sharing a pot of tea and a list.

Your list is going to be impressive. Resist the urge to add more than five items. Saturn and Virgo together can talk you into overachieving. Instead, choose the item that helps someone else level up and do it first. The rest follow easily. Around sunset, walk to the shore and watch the water sort the pebbles. It has been organising them for centuries and it is still not finished. Neither are you, and that is fine.
nancy.mission: Make a to-do list with exactly five items and cross one off within ten minutes of writing it.
nancy.omen: Neatly stacked stones on a beach or path. It means your patience is paying off quietly.

together.text: Each choose one item to finish today and tell the other what it is by 9 am. Check in at 6 pm with a single word: done, close, or nope. Virgo is keeping score, but it grades on a gentle curve.

title: The Quest for the Perfect Pebble
skyStory: Eighty-seven percent full and still in Virgo, the moon is now polishing every pebble on the beach, one at a time, with a soft cloth. It knows this will take forever. It does not care. Saturn admires the dedication. Mars offers a power tool. The moon declines politely and keeps polishing.

reading: Saturday energy, Virgo moon. The Tiger wants to roam, so roam with a purpose: go somewhere outside, beach, park, woods, and look for one perfect stone. Not good. Perfect.

It will take longer than you think. You will pick up about twenty. Fine. The search is the point. When you find it, hold it in your left hand, the receiving side, and notice how it settles. The [[Six of Pentacles]] says you can receive even from a rock. Bring it home, set it beside the onyx, and let the two of them get acquainted overnight.
joel.mission: Hunt for one perfect pebble outdoors, and do not stop until it feels right in your palm.
joel.omen: A heart-shaped stone, leaf, or puddle. It means today's search is already rewarded, so slow down.

reading: The Wood Rat in you is a collector, and the Virgo moon approves. Spend part of the day looking through something you have collected, photos, notes, rings, shells, and choose a favourite.

Tell its story to yourself out loud, as if narrating a nature documentary. The mother of pearl on your ring finger will catch the light right at the best part. Around 5 pm, a memory will surface, a good one, from a spring long ago. Write two lines about it. You do not have to share them. The [[Page of Cups]] is grinning at you from a tide pool, holding up a fish, delighted.
nancy.mission: Choose one favourite object from a collection and narrate its history aloud like a nature documentary.
nancy.omen: A shell or bead that catches the light at the perfect moment. It means a memory is knocking, so let it in.

together.text: Joel finds a pebble, Nancy picks a favourite treasure. Swap photos tonight and each write one sentence about what the other's object would say if it could talk. The Virgo moon will have edited both sentences for grammar by morning.

title: The Last Polish Before the Party
skyStory: Ninety-four percent full, the moon is almost round, still in Virgo, doing a final sweep of the sky before tomorrow's big night. It has dusted the clouds, straightened the constellations, and hung a sign that says nearly ready. Saturn is checking the guest list. Mars is impatient and keeps opening the front door to peek.

reading: The full moon is a day away, and today is for preparation. Clear a spot on a windowsill where the ruby and onyx can sit side by side tomorrow night. Wipe it down. Make it ceremonial.

Sunday chores take on a new glow when you know there is a party coming. Do one thing that makes the cabin feel ready for a guest, even if the only guest is the moon. Around 3 pm you will have a sudden urge to start something big. The [[Temperance]] angel says pour slowly from one cup to the other. Start tomorrow. Tonight, sit by the fire and let the anticipation build.
joel.mission: Prepare a clean, clear spot on a windowsill facing the eastern sky for tomorrow night's moonlight.
joel.omen: A glimpse of the nearly full moon in daylight. It means the recharge is coming, so get ready.

reading: You will have that Sunday feeling, where the week has not started but your brain has. Let Virgo help: spend twenty minutes planning, then put the planner away and walk to the water.

The shore is busy with spring birds today, sandpipers running back and forth like they forgot something. Watch them for five minutes. They do not rush the tide, they just keep up with it. That is your lesson. Tonight, pick the spot where your ruby will sit under the moon tomorrow. It deserves a good view. Maybe the same window where you watched the winter solstice light come back.
nancy.mission: Watch shorebirds or any birds for five full minutes and give each one a job title.
nancy.omen: A bird running along the waterline. It means keep pace, do not rush, and the tide works for you.
nancy.elementWhy: plant your feet before the party

together.text: Each prepare a moonlit spot for your stones tomorrow, and send a photo of it tonight. Rate each other's set-up on vibes alone. The Virgo moon has already rated both as excellent but needs one more polish.

title: The Full Moon Recharge Begins
skyStory: The full moon arrives, ninety-eight percent bright, gliding into Libra, the sign of the scales and perfect balance. Libra wants everything paired and even: day with night, fire with mountain, ruby with onyx. The marshes are singing. Saturn and Mars, who usually argue, are sharing a bench and nodding. Tonight, everything is in balance.

reading: Full Moon Recharge, part one. After dark, set your onyx bracelet on the windowsill you prepared, right where the moonlight lands. Set something red beside it to stand in for the ruby. Libra loves a pair.

While the stones soak up the light, think about what you give and what you receive, and whether the scale tips too far one way. You know which way it tips. The [[Justice]] card weighs things honestly, and it says you can add a little more receiving to the pan. Ask for one small thing tomorrow. For now, stand by the window for a minute and let the moon look at you. It likes what it sees.
joel.mission: Set the onyx bracelet in moonlight after dark and leave it there until morning without peeking.
joel.omen: A perfectly balanced object, like a stick on a fence or a cup on a ledge. It means your scales are leveling.

reading: Full moon over the water is your kind of magic. Go to the shore after dark if you can, or to the window if you cannot, and watch the light lay a silver road across the waves.

Then set your ruby on the sill next to your onyx bracelet. Capricorn and Libra are both cardinal signs, starters and leaders, and tonight they are shaking hands. The [[Six of Swords]] glides along that silver road, and the far shore is closer than it was in January. You can see the trees on it. Make a wish, a small and specific one, and say it once into the dark.
nancy.mission: Set the ruby beside the onyx in moonlight and make one specific, small wish out loud.
nancy.omen: A silver path of moonlight on water or a wet road. It means the crossing is nearly done.

together.text: Full Moon Recharge, night one. Set your stones out at the same time, 9:00 pm, and send a single photo of the windowsill. The Libra moon will balance the light between both houses, exactly even, like scales. Tomorrow, the peak.

title: The Night the Owls Agreed
skyStory: One hundred percent. The moon is perfectly round, perfectly full, sitting in the very centre of Libra's scales. Every star is holding its breath. The peepers stop for one beat, all at once, then start again. Saturn and Mars clink mugs. Libra says nothing, because nothing needs saying when everything is balanced. Tonight the moon sends signs in pairs.

reading: Peak full moon, Recharge part two. Your onyx has been bathing for a full night and now it is time for the second round. Before you set it back out, wear it on your right wrist for one hour, the giving side, and send all that moonlit strength to Nancy.

Around 10:10 pm, standing outside the cabin, you will hear an owl call twice. Wait. A second owl will answer from the other side of the woods, exactly twice. At that same minute, a long way off, Nancy will hear the same. Don't even scream. Just stand there grinning like a fool in the moonlight. [[The Star]] card says hope is answering hope.
joel.mission: Wear the onyx on your right wrist for one full hour this evening, then return it to the moonlit sill.
joel.omen: Two owls calling back and forth. It means the bond is humming at full strength tonight.

reading: Full moon in Libra, peak brightness, and your ruby has soaked up a night of it. Hold it up to the window before you set it back out. The silver mount will glow and the stone will look almost purple.

You are going to hear something tonight around 10:10 pm: two owls, one calling, one answering. The Wood Rat knows owls are wise and a little bit mischievous. Count the calls. Then check your phone. Joel will have heard the same pair at the same minute. ΔΕΣ, written across two skies. Tell the story at breakfast with both hands. It will be your best one this month.
nancy.mission: Stand outside or at an open window at 10:10 pm for five minutes and count every sound you hear.
nancy.omen: An owl call answered by another. It means your intuition, Life Path 11, is running perfectly tonight.

together.text: DES night and peak recharge. Both listen outside at 10:10 pm, then compare what you heard, owl for owl. If the counts match, you are officially unstoppable this spring. Leave the stones under the moon until sunrise.

title: The Scorpion Collects the Stones
skyStory: Still full at ninety-nine percent, the moon has slipped out of Libra's tidy scales and into Scorpio, the sign of secrets, deep water and things whispered after midnight. Scorpio walks along every windowsill, inspecting the charged stones, approving. It leaves a single damp footprint as a signature. Saturn pretends not to see. Mars thinks it is extremely cool.

reading: Bring the onyx in from the sill this morning and notice the weight. It feels heavier after two nights of moon, or at least the story says so, and the story is the point.

Scorpio wants depth today, not breadth. Instead of chatting with ten people, have one real conversation, the kind where you ask a second question after the first answer. Life Path 3 can talk to anyone, but today, listen more than you speak. [[The Hermit]] card holds up a lantern in your direction. Somewhere in that quiet chat is the answer to a question you have not asked out loud yet.
joel.mission: In one conversation today, ask a follow-up question to every answer, at least three deep.
joel.omen: A single glove or key lying in a puddle. It means something hidden wants to be found, so look closer.

reading: Slip the ruby back on your right pinky this morning and feel it hum. Two nights in the moon have given it opinions, and today it will nudge you toward the true thing in every room.

Scorpio loves a secret and so does the Wood Rat. Somebody will confide in you around midday, nothing heavy, just a small private hope. Keep it like a pearl in a shell. Later, write down one secret wish of your own on a slip of paper and tuck it in your pocket. Carry it all day. By evening it will feel less like a secret and more like a plan.
nancy.mission: Write one private wish on a slip of paper and carry it in your pocket until bedtime.
nancy.omen: A dark bird, crow or raven, watching from a wire. It means a secret is safe with you, and the sky knows it.

together.text: Bring the stones in from the window and share one thing you are letting go of now that the recharge is done. One sentence each, no follow-up questions allowed. Scorpio will keep both sentences in a locked box at the bottom of the sea.

title: The Five Elements Roll Call
skyStory: Ninety-seven percent and still full in Scorpio, the moon looks down on a planet celebrating itself today. Scorpio, a water sign, approves of all the rivers. Every element is standing in a line for roll call: earth, fire, water, wind and heart. The moon has a clipboard borrowed from Virgo. Saturn calls the names. Mars answers for everyone.

reading: It is a day for the whole planet, and you get to be one of its champions. Your five-ring friend has the elements covered with stones. You have the Fire Tiger. Bring the spark: one action today that helps the earth, however small.

Pick up three pieces of litter on your walk. Fix a dripping tap. Plant a single seed in a pot by the window. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] is out in the fields today, slow and steady, planting rows. You do not need to save the world before lunch. You just need to be one good link in the chain. Life Path 3 can rally others too, so tell someone what you did.
joel.mission: Pick up three pieces of litter during your walk today and give each one a dramatic farewell.
joel.omen: A green shoot pushing through a crack in the pavement. It means small efforts break through big barriers.

reading: Today is your day to be the captain of the elements. Look at your hands: onyx for earth, ruby for fire, mother of pearl for water, diamonds for wind, and the ruby again for heart. You are wearing a whole team.

Touch each stone once this morning, naming its element out loud. It is silly. It is also lovely. Then pick one element to serve today. Water: tidy up a stretch of shoreline. Earth: plant something. Wind: open every window and let spring in. [[The World]] card, complete and whole, is spinning in your direction today, and it looks a lot like a hand with five rings on it.
nancy.mission: Touch each of your five stones in turn, saying its element aloud, before you leave home.
nancy.omen: A rainbow in a puddle, sprinkler or window. It means all five elements are aligned today.

together.text: Assemble the team. Each choose one of the five elements and do one small kind thing for the planet in its name. Report back with the element and the deed. Five rings, one tiger, one rat and a whole planet, cheering quietly.

title: The Archer Packs a Picnic
skyStory: The moon has started to wane, ninety-two percent and gently shrinking, and has trotted into Sagittarius, the archer, who would very much like to go on an adventure, preferably with snacks. Sagittarius is packing a picnic basket with no clear destination. Saturn suggests a map. Mars suggests just going. The archer throws the map in the basket and leaves.

reading: Fire moon in a fire sign, and the Tiger wants to roam. Find twenty minutes today to go somewhere you have never been, even if it is just the end of a road you always drive past.

Bring something to eat, because Sagittarius believes every expedition deserves a snack. Sit somewhere new and look around like an explorer who just discovered a continent. Around 4 pm, notice three things you have never seen before within a short walk of your usual path. The [[Eight of Wands]] fly overhead, eight arrows all heading the same direction, fast and true. Follow where they point.
joel.mission: Take a turn down a road or path you have never explored, and stop for a snack at the end.
joel.omen: An arrow drawn in chalk or painted on a sign. It means follow your curiosity today, it knows the way.

reading: The archer moon wants you to share a meal with someone today, and to tell a story while you do. Sagittarius is the storyteller's moon, wandering and generous and a little bit loud.

Pick a favourite person, a favourite table, and an excuse. Bring your best story, the one with a twist at the end. Your hands will do the rest. Around 7 pm, the conversation will turn to dreams and places you want to see. Name one out loud. The [[Three of Cups]] is raising a glass somewhere nearby, celebrating friendship and the simple joy of a shared table.
nancy.mission: Invite someone to share a meal or snack, and tell them the best story you know.
nancy.omen: Someone laughing loudly at the next table. It means your joy is contagious today, so spread it.

together.text: Each eat one thing today you have never tasted before, no matter how small, and describe it to the other using only three adjectives. The archer moon will try to guess what it was. It will guess wrong and be delighted.

title: The Kite Without a String
skyStory: Eighty-six percent and waning, the moon is still in Sagittarius, flying a kite that has somehow lost its string and is just hanging in the sky by sheer optimism. The archer insists it was always meant to fly free. Saturn is horrified. Mars is thrilled. The kite does a loop and seems to agree with Mars.

reading: Saturday and Sagittarius, the perfect combination for a free-range afternoon. Leave the plan at home. Wander. Let the day decide.

Around 1 pm, a spring breeze will carry a smell, cut grass or salt or woodsmoke, and you will remember something from when you were small. Follow that memory. Do one thing your younger self would have loved: climb something low, skip a stone, fly something, build a fort out of couch cushions. [[The Fool]] is stepping off a low ledge into the open sky today, with a little dog yapping happily behind him.
joel.mission: Do one thing your eight-year-old self would have loved, and do it with full commitment.
joel.omen: A kite or balloon high in the sky. It means let one worry go today, it will float away on its own.

reading: Today the Wood Rat goes exploring. Sagittarius wants you out of the burrow and somewhere new. Pick a direction, any direction, and walk for twenty minutes without a destination.

You will notice things only you would notice: a tiny door at the base of a tree, a forgotten bench with a carved name, a window display arranged with real love. Take a mental photograph of each. When you get home, tell someone about the best one with full storytelling hands. The archer moon loves your gift for spotting wonder in ordinary corners, and it is aiming its arrows at all of them today.
nancy.mission: Walk for twenty minutes in a random direction and find three things nobody else would notice.
nancy.omen: A tiny door or nook in an unlikely place. It means hidden wonders are close by today, keep looking.

together.text: Each send the other one photo of the most whimsical thing you find on today's wander, a door, a sign, a strangely shaped cloud. No caption allowed. The archer moon will award a ribbon for most delightful find.

title: The Goat Climbs Home
skyStory: Seventy-nine percent and waning, the moon has climbed into Capricorn, Nancy's own sign, a sure-footed sea-goat picking its way up the mountain. Saturn, who rules Capricorn, has put on a cozy sweater and made tea for the guest. The goat settles in at the summit, looks out over the shore, and says nothing. It does not need to.

reading: The moon is visiting Nancy's sign, and some of her mountain steadiness rubs off on you. Notice it. You will feel unusually calm around 10 am, like a fire banked properly in the cabin stove.

Use the calm. Tackle the task that requires patience, the one you keep starting and abandoning. Do it the Capricorn way: slow, one handhold at a time, no shortcuts. The [[Knight of Wands]] in your spread is about aiming the fire, and today you aim it like a laser, not a flamethrower. Later, send Nancy a message thanking her for lending you the mountain for the day. She will know what you mean.
joel.mission: Spend thirty minutes on one patient task with no distractions, like climbing a mountain step by step.
joel.omen: A goat, ram, or any horned animal picture in an unexpected place. It means patience is your power today.

reading: Welcome home, Mountain. The moon is in your sign, and it brought the whole family: Saturn in his sweater, the sea-goat at the summit, the shore laid out below. You will feel like yourself in the best possible way.

This is a day for you to set a goal and climb toward it, small and steady. Make one decision you have been putting off, a little one, a choice between two colours or two routes. Decide it before noon. Capricorns feel taller after a good decision. Around 5 pm, someone will remark on how calm you seem. Take it as a compliment. It is one.
nancy.mission: Make one small decision before noon that you have been putting off, and do not reconsider it.
nancy.omen: A mountain on a sign, a postcard, or a screen. It means you are exactly where you should be today.

together.text: The moon is in Nancy's sign, so Nancy picks a small goal for the two of you this week, and Joel must cheer for it like a crowd at the finish line. Saturn is making tea for both of you. The goat is pleased.

title: The Slow and Steady Monday
skyStory: The waning gibbous moon, seventy-one percent lit, lingers in Capricorn like a guest who loves the cabin too much to leave. Saturn has shown it the woodpile. The sea-goat has rearranged the bookshelf by height. Mars is impatient to get going. Capricorn reminds everyone that mountains were not built in a day, and neither are Mondays.

reading: Monday with the moon in Capricorn means structure wins. Make a plan for the week, but keep it short: three things, written on a card you can carry in your pocket.

Your instinct is to write ten. Do not. Three. The Capricorn moon likes things that are achievable and solid. Around 2 pm, you will be tempted by a shiny new idea. Write it on the back of the card and let it wait. Saturn says the shiny thing will still be shiny next week. The [[Four of Pentacles]] holds on tight to what matters, and today what matters is finishing.
joel.mission: Write your three big tasks for the week on an index card, then keep it tucked away on you all day.
joel.omen: A neatly stacked woodpile or row of bricks. It means steady building today will pay off.

reading: Saturn is still wearing the sweater on day two of your Capricorn moon. You are steady, clear and quietly unstoppable. The Wood Rat feels sharp as a tack.

Someone will try to rush you today. Do not let them. Your pace is your power. Life Path 11 means your intuition is extra loud right now, so if something feels off about a plan, say so, kindly but firmly. You will be right. Around 6 pm, take a walk near water and let your mind wander. A good idea is waiting for you near the shore.
nancy.mission: When someone rushes you today, take one deliberate breath before responding, then answer at your own pace.
nancy.omen: A sea-bird gliding without flapping. It means effortless progress is possible, so slow down and coast.

together.text: Share your three weekly goals with each other by noon. At the end of the week, check in. Saturn has made a little chart and will be very proud of progress, even partial. The goat moon recommends a reward for finishing.

title: The Day the Goats Appeared
skyStory: Last quarter, sixty-two percent, and the moon is still in Capricorn, the sea-goat, making a final circuit of the summit before it leaves. Capricorn likes to say goodbye with a gift. Tonight the gift is goats. Many goats. In pictures, on signs, in conversation. Saturn denies arranging this. The goat is smirking.

reading: Goats will be everywhere today. A goat on a cheese label, a goat on a coffee mug, someone saying I am such a goat about something. Count them. By 3 pm, you will hit seven.

Seven is the magic number today, because Nancy, born under the sea-goat, will have counted exactly seven too. Don't even scream. The Capricorn moon is waving goodbye with both hooves. When you compare notes, the Tiger will be pleased. Sometimes the universe just wants to remind you that the mountain is never far. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] turns, and it lands on the same spot twice.
joel.mission: Count every goat you see or hear about today, in any form, and report the total at dusk.
joel.omen: A real live goat or a picture of one before 9 am. It means the count is on, so pay attention.

reading: The sea-goat moon is leaving your sign tonight, and it wants to give you something before it goes. You will notice goats today, in places goats should not be, on signs, in books, in a stranger's joke.

Count them. The Wood Rat counts everything anyway. You will reach seven by late afternoon. Then text Joel, and he will have exactly seven too. ΔΕΣ. Capricorn and Aries, mountain and fire, counting goats in perfect sync. Tell the story at dinner with both hands making little horns. Everyone at the table will look at you like you have lost the plot, and that is perfect.
nancy.mission: Count goats all day and make little horns with your fingers each time you spot one.
nancy.omen: A goat on a sign or label you have walked past a hundred times. It means the universe is in on the joke.

together.text: DES day. Count goats all day, any kind: drawn, spoken, carved, real. Compare totals at sunset. If they match, the sea-goat leaves Capricorn with a satisfied bleat. If they do not, recount, because it is probably seven.

title: The Inventor's Wednesday
skyStory: At fifty-two percent, half lit and fading, the moon has drifted out of Capricorn into Aquarius, the inventor, the rebel, the sign that builds a robot to water its plants. Aquarius has a garage full of contraptions and a head full of better ones. Saturn co-rules here and is quietly impressed. Mars wants to press every button.

reading: Aquarius is the moon of inventions, and you are a builder. Today, tinker. Take something apart to see how it works, or put two odd things together to see what happens.

It does not have to be useful. That is the point. Around 11 am, an idea for a small improvement will pop into your head: a better hook, a smarter shelf, a gadget nobody asked for. Sketch it on a napkin. [[The Magician]] has all four tools on his table today, and so do you. Build a prototype from things around the cabin before supper. Then name it something ridiculous.
joel.mission: Invent one small useless gadget from household items, name it, and demonstrate it to someone.
joel.omen: A strange machine or contraption in a yard or window. It means your creativity is fully charged today.

reading: The inventor moon is here, and it wants you to rethink something you have always done the same way. Your morning routine, the route to work, the way you fold towels. Change one thing.

It will feel odd at first. The Wood Rat loves a new trail through familiar woods. By evening, you might decide the new way is better. Or not. Either way, you learned something. Around 3 pm, help someone solve a problem with a sideways idea, one nobody else thought of. Aquarius loves an unexpected answer, and Life Path 11 is full of them.
nancy.mission: Change one small habit today, like the order you get ready, and notice how it feels.
nancy.omen: Something used in an unusual way, a teacup as a planter or a boot as a doorstop. It means try a new approach.

together.text: Invent a secret handshake you can do over video call, at least four moves long, including one that involves the stones. Practise it once tonight. The Aquarius moon will rate it for originality and award bonus points for absurdity.

title: The Rowboat at Low Tide
skyStory: Forty-three percent and waning, the moon is still in Aquarius, rowing a small boat through the clouds with a lantern on the bow. Aquarius is a visionary, but tonight it is in a gentle mood. It is just rowing, looking at the stars, wondering about the far shore. Saturn holds the other oar. Mars is asleep in the stern.

reading: Some days the Tiger hunts. Today, the Tiger helps someone else row. Look around: who in your life is in the middle of a crossing, a change, a long project, a hard week?

Offer to take the oar for a while. Not a huge favour, just a small one: run an errand, send a cheerful message, listen to them vent for ten minutes. The [[Six of Swords]] is Nancy's card, but today it is yours too, because you are the one in the boat with the extra oar. Around 8 pm, switch your onyx to your right wrist for an hour and send that steady strength to her, too.
joel.mission: Do one small, unasked favour for someone who is in the middle of something hard.
joel.omen: A rowboat, canoe or kayak pulled up on a shore. It means someone needs your help to cross.

reading: Low tide at the shore today, and the rocks are showing. The water is calm. The boat you have been rowing since January feels lighter now. You may not see the far shore yet, but you can smell the pine trees on it.

Today, let Joel take an oar. He will offer help in some form before evening: a message, a joke, a suggestion. Say yes. You do not always have to row alone, Mountain. Around 8 pm, look at your ruby and feel a little warmth from it. That is him, switching wrists. The crossing is nearly done.
nancy.mission: Accept the first offer of help you receive today, no matter how small, and say thank you.
nancy.omen: Calm water at low tide, showing rocks. It means the crossing is easier now, and the end is near.

together.text: At 8 pm, Joel switches the onyx to his right wrist, and Nancy holds the ruby up to the light. One hour, one message each: a single word describing how the crossing feels right now. The Aquarius moon rows quietly between you.

title: The Eve of May Parade
skyStory: The last day of April, and the moon is a third lit, waning in Aquarius, holding a tiny parade for the end of the month. Every star has a kazoo. The peepers are the marching band. Saturn has made a banner that says goodbye mud season, hello May. Mars is leading the parade in a paper crown.

reading: April was a whole season in one month: pranks, fog, puddles, crocuses, two uncanny coincidences with Nancy, a full moon, and a lot of goats. Take a moment to look back on it before you rush ahead.

Write down three moments from April that made you grin. Keep it short: three lines, three moments. Life Path 3 loves telling a story, and this is your highlight reel. Around 7 pm, step outside the cabin and listen to the peepers one more time. They are louder than ever. They are the sound of May, warming up backstage. The [[Ten of Wands]] can finally put down the bundle. You carried it well.
joel.mission: Write a three-line highlight reel of April and read it aloud to the cabin walls.
joel.omen: A blossom opening on a branch. It means the next season is starting, and you are ready for it.

reading: The shore is greening. You can see it in the reeds and the moss on the rocks. April has done its slow, steady work, the way you do, and now May is waiting just offstage.

Write down three April stories you want to remember. One funny, one strange, one sweet. Tell one of them to someone tonight, with your hands dancing, because a story is not finished until someone hears it. The Wood Rat knows which one gets the biggest laugh. Around 9 pm, set the ruby on the windowsill one last time this month, a little thank you to the waning moon for its company.
nancy.mission: Write three April stories, one funny, one strange, one sweet, and tell one aloud tonight.
nancy.omen: Moss turning bright green on a rock. It means steady growth is showing, even if it is slow.

together.text: Swap your April highlight reels tonight, three lines each. Pick a favourite moment from the other's list and tell them why it made you grin. The Aquarius moon is playing a kazoo. Saturn is crying a tiny bit. May begins tomorrow.
